title: About BART
relevance: Current official system-facts source stating that BART operates in five counties with 131 miles of track and 50 stations.
notes: Useful current system-scope source showing the provider is multi-county, not a Contra Costa-only police agency.

title: BART Police
relevance: Current official BART police page describing a single BART Police Department whose mission is safety within the transit system.
notes: Good current identity source for one department serving the transit system.

title: Know Your Zone / BART Police Zone Map
relevance: Current official police zone map showing one BART police command structure spanning the network, including multiple Contra Costa stations and beats.
notes: Useful for rejecting single-city proxies inside Contra Costa and for showing current Contra Costa coverage is part of one systemwide police map.

title: BART Police Department Strategic Plan 2023-2027
relevance: Current official police PDF stating BART PD provides police services 24/7 for the district and that the district is a 131-mile 50-station system servicing five counties.
notes: Best current police-specific source showing one districtwide department rather than separate county departments.

title: BART Police Department Report
relevance: Official BART police report stating BART PD is the primary law-enforcement authority for the BART District including trackway, stations, and parking stalls spanning Alameda, Contra Costa, San Francisco, and San Mateo Counties.
notes: Strong property-scope source showing the geography is BART property, not general county territory.

title: BART Police Department Monthly Report January 2026
relevance: Current official BART police report with a Systemwide section and separate Contra Costa County performance pages inside the same Bay Area Rapid Transit Police Department report.
notes: Key source showing Contra Costa is an active county reporting slice within one department, not a separate police agency.

title: California Penal Code Section 830.33
relevance: Official statute tying BART peace-officer authority to enforcement in or about district-owned, operated, or administered property and related duties involving district patrons, employees, and properties.
notes: Core legal basis for rejecting countywide or placewide proxying.

title: California Public Utilities Code Section 99170
relevance: Official statute governing conduct on transit-district property and on facilities where BART owes policing responsibilities to a local government under agreement.
notes: Important for the exact include/exclude boundary of a BART custom footprint.

title: FBI Crime in the United States 2019 California table 81
relevance: Official FBI public table listing 'San Francisco Bay Area Rapid Transit' with a distinct 'Contra Costa County' unit row.
notes: Useful public official roster-style evidence that the Contra Costa slice existed as a named reporting unit, without implying a separate county police department.

title: FBI Hate Crime Statistics 2018 California table 13
relevance: Official FBI public table showing San Francisco Bay Area Rapid Transit broken into Alameda County, Contra Costa County, and Santa Clara Transit District rows.
notes: Useful public evidence that BART county/unit slicing is longstanding and administrative.

title: Pittsburg/Bay Point BART Station Area Specific Plan DEIR
publisher: Contra Costa County / City of Pittsburg / Bay Area Rapid Transit District
relevance: County/public planning document stating Contra Costa County Sheriff serves Bay Point, Pittsburg Police serves Pittsburg, and BART provides police services to the Pittsburg/Bay Point BART Station; it further states BART police is responsible for security and law enforcement on BART-owned properties.
notes: Best county/public source for rejecting county or city proxies and for showing BART policing follows BART property inside Contra Costa.

title: 2024 FBI-derived BART roster rows
relevance: Local roster evidence showing active 2024 BART rows for Alameda, Contra Costa, San Francisco, San Mateo, and Santa Clara counties.
notes: Current repo evidence that the county-tagged BART slices remain active in 2024.
